picks.rationale: The San Diego Padres have a clear starting pitching advantage with newly acquired Casey Mize making his debut, while Arizona's Mitch Bratt holds a 5.23 ERA. San Diego has won 9 of their last 11 games against National League opponents and has covered the run line in 9 of their last 10 road games against NL opponents. Public money has heavily favored the Padres on the moneyline, reaching as high as 94% of dollars wagered, indicating sharp action. The Padres also hold a 4-1 record in their last 5 head-to-head matchups against the Diamondbacks.

The Cincinnati Reds are in strong recent form, winning four of their last five games, including the series opener against the Athletics. Conversely, the Athletics have lost six straight games. Public money has consistently backed Cincinnati on the moneyline, reaching as high as 94% of dollars wagered. The Reds also hold a significant team pitching edge with a 4.40 ERA and 1.41 WHIP compared to the Athletics' 5.42 ERA and 1.50 WHIP.

The Milwaukee Brewers boast a strong home record of 37-21 and a dominant overall record of 70-43, placing them atop the NL Central. They have a significant pitching advantage with Kyle Harrison, who is lined up to return and start, while the Pirates' Mitch Keller is on the 60-day injured list. The Brewers have the deeper lineup and a stronger late-game structure, which is crucial in close matchups. Public money has shifted between both sides, but the Brewers remain a modest home favorite at a reasonable price.

Both starting pitchers, Reid Detmers for the Angels and Trevor Rogers for the Orioles, have been in good form, with Detmers allowing only three runs in his last 16 innings and Rogers giving up two runs or less in seven of his last eight starts. Both teams have struggled against left-handed pitching recently, averaging just 4.7 runs per game combined in their last five games against southpaws. The Angels and Orioles have also gone 6-0-1 to the under in their last seven games combined, and their previous game had only four total runs.

The Detroit Tigers offense is currently on a hot streak, entering this game on a four-game winning streak and coming off an 8-0 victory in the series opener. Seattle's probable starter, Bryan Woo, has struggled recently with an ERA above 4.50, including a 6.75 ERA in his last disaster stretch. The Mariners' offense has also shown the ability to put up runs, going over the total in seven of their last ten games. With Detroit likely deploying a bullpen game, and both teams trending towards high-scoring affairs, the over is a strong play.
